title: Running, Debugging & Next Steps 🐞
description: Master essential dev commands, debug in the browser, and preview your learning path.

slides.title: Essential CLI Commands 🛠️
slides.content:
## Daily Drivers

* `ng serve` – development server with live reload.
* `ng generate component <name>` – create a new component (shorthand: `ng g c`).
* `ng build` – compile app for production (output in `dist/`).
* `ng test` – run unit tests.
* `ng lint` – check code quality.

Use `ng help` to see all available commands.

quizData.question: Which command creates a new component called 'header'?
quizData.explanation: `ng generate component header` (or `ng g c header`) scaffolds a new component.

slides.title: Debugging Like a Pro 🔍
slides.content:
## Browser Developer Tools

1. **Open DevTools** (F12 or right‑click > Inspect).
2. Go to the **Console** tab to see logs and errors.
3. Use `console.log()` in your TypeScript code (it appears here).
4. The **Sources** tab lets you set breakpoints in your .ts files (thanks to source maps).

Angular DevTools extension (Chrome/Firefox) gives you a component tree and profiler.

slides.title: Common Error ⚠️
slides.content:
## “Port 4200 is already in use”

If another `ng serve` is running, you’ll see this. Either stop the other instance or use a different port:

```bash
ng serve --port 4500
```

quizData.question: The Angular CLI automatically reloads the browser when you save a file.
quizData.explanation: `ng serve` watches your files and triggers a browser reload when changes are detected.
